newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Hubco gets notice from Pakistan utility.
newsitem.headline: Hubco gets notice from Pakistan utility.

text.p: Pakistan's Hub Power Co Ltd (Hubco) said on Friday it had received a notice from the state-run Water and Power Development Authority (WAPDA).
Hubco, which earlier denied it had received any such notice, did not immediately confirm a newspaper report on Friday that WAPDA had threatened to terminate its power purchase agreement.
A spokesman for Hubco, in which Britain's National Power and Saudi Arabia's Xenel Industries Ltd have major stakes, said the company had received the notice and was now studying it.
The News daily said WAPDA had accused Hubco of tampering with meters showing how much power WAPDA was getting from Hubco. It said WAPDA had given Hubco 30 days to "prove its innocence".
Water and Power Minister Nisar Ali Khan declined to comment on the issue at a news conference in Islamabad.
Hubco's 10-rupee stock closed 0.10 rupee down at 37.80 at the Karachi bourse on Friday. The $1.5 billion 1,292-megawatt Hubco plant near Karachi, was completed in February.
